spec_says: rv_timer_Design_Specification.md:604-606 (INT-INTG-002): "When i_a_intg_flip is 1, bit 0 of a_user.cmd_intg is inverted. The request then has a command integrity error: a fatal TL-UL bus integrity fault ..., which triggers the fatal_fault alert (section 5)." This does not say the request must first be accepted. D-010, line 668 (RT-8-16): "o_alert shall pulse no later than 16 cycles after the request with i_a_intg_flip = 1 is accepted". That is an upper bound measured from acceptance. It does not forbid an earlier alert. D-009, line 667 (RT-8-14) bounds alert pulses caused by ALERT_TEST writes "with no other alert cause". The contract (contract.json:302) is what moves the start of the exemption to acceptance: "flip_seen: set at the acceptance edge of any request with i_a_intg_flip=1". D-014, line 672, lets the bench issue requests without assuming o_a_ready=1, so presenting a request while a_ready=0 is legal.
verification_does: nnc_chk_alert.sv:66 defines `flip_now_w = flip_seen || (acc_w && i_a_intg_flip)`, and line 81 sets flip_seen only `if (acc_w && i_a_intg_flip)`. A flip request that is presented (i_a_valid=1) but not yet accepted, or never accepted, does not stop the check. Lines 112-115 then require q_cnt+qual_w-qerr >= a_cnt+1 and a recent qualifying write for every o_alert pulse.
what_to_change: B (recommended): in nnc_chk_alert.sv, set flip_seen and flip_now_w at any edge with rst_ni=1, i_a_valid=1 and i_a_intg_flip=1, not only on acc_w, and update the contract text of CHK-003 (contract.json:302) to match. Review the same acceptance-based disable in the other checks: nnc_chk_intr.sv:59 `dis = seen_flip || (acc && i_a_intg_flip)`, and the flip disables of CHK-005, CHK-009, CHK-010 and CHK-012. C: if the designer wants the alert tied strictly to acceptance, record that as a new D-xxx decision in section 8. Do not add an environment assumption that forbids flip requests while a_ready=0: the spec does not support it.

spec_says: D-005, rv_timer_Design_Specification.md:663 (RT-8-07): "o_intr_timer_expired shall equal IS_0 AND IE_0 except in the 2 cycles after either changes." The comportability rule CP-T1.8.6-04 says the same: "The output of the INTR_STATE register becomes the outgoing interrupt to the processor after masking (ANDing) with the value of INTR_ENABLE." IE_0 is the rw field at bit 0, and bits 31:1 are reserved (RT-T5.4.1-01). Register tool, opentitan_register_tool.md:689-695: errors only for "writes of size smaller than register size" ("The width of the register is determined by the location of its fields") and for sub-32b writes that are not word-aligned. INTR_ENABLE0 has width 1, so an aligned 16-bit write is legal and takes effect. D-013 (line 671): "Non-contiguous masks and other sub-word cases are not checked". This says they are not checked; it does not say they are excluded. INT-TL-003 (lines 594-595) makes such requests legal stimulus.
verification_does: nnc_chk_intr.sv:68-70 updates ie only for writes to 0x100 with (a_size=2, mask 1111) or (a_size=0, mask 0001). The update happens at the D beat with d_error=0 (line 104). Line 61 tracks any write to 0x100 in c100/dw0..dw2 only until its D beat plus 2 edges. After that, ie is assumed to still hold its old value (0) even though an unmodelled, error-free write to 0x100 may have changed IE_0. The assertion at lines 113-114 then requires o_intr_timer_expired=0. The contract text (contract.json:316) defines ie the same way, restricted to these two write kinds.
what_to_change: B (recommended), two choices. (1) In nnc_chk_intr.sv:68-70, let any error-free write (opcode 0/1, intg_flip=0, instr=0) to 0x100 with i_a_mask[0]=1 update ie from i_a_data[0] at its D beat. This matches the register-tool width rule and PERMIT 0001. (2) More conservatively, add an 'ie_unknown' flag that is set at the error-free D beat of any write to 0x100 that is not one of the modelled kinds. It disables CHK-004 until the next modelled write or reset. Update the contract's ie definition (contract.json:316) to match. Do not add an environment assumption that forbids half-word or other sub-word writes to 0x100: INT-TL-003 makes them legal stimulus. A side note, not the cause here: the checker's in-order queue (rp/wp FIFO) assumes in-order responses.
